account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry dated 16 January 2026 summarizes Ghanaian reports that the Ghana Revenue Authority launched Publican AI. That is a trade data analytics platform to identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation. MyJoy’s original launch report attributes GH¢15 million in recovered revenue from five companies to the pilot. The underlying recovery ledger is not published in the inspected reports. The entry is classified as an AI Incident with the harm type economic harm to property interests. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would give 100 percent coverage of assessment. He said that assessments could be completed within five minutes instead of about two hours. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. That article cites no realized recovery. The vendor is described only as a Cyprus-based firm.

ai_role.statement: Neither source describes how the analytics identify undervaluation or what share of the claimed recovery the system produced. The system is vendor-built and deployed by the GRA.

claim_basis: Sources: three independent news reports and a registry entry. The cited evidence includes no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.

fields.account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry dated 16 January 2026 summarizes Ghanaian reports that the Ghana Revenue Authority launched Publican AI. That is a trade data analytics platform to identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation. MyJoy’s original launch report attributes GH¢15 million in recovered revenue from five companies to the pilot. The underlying recovery ledger is not published in the inspected reports. The entry is classified as an AI Incident with the harm type economic harm to property interests. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would give 100 percent coverage of assessment. He said that assessments could be completed within five minutes instead of about two hours. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. That article cites no realized recovery. The vendor is described only as a Cyprus-based firm.
